items.title: North Korea touts BBQ restaurant boom, but sceptics dismiss it as propaganda
items.desc: North Korea has announced more than a dozen new barbecue restaurants since September, but analysts say the fanfare is aimed at projecting prosperity while food insecurity remains widespread.

items.title: Dashain gone, Tihar uncertain: Nepali workers stranded in Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks disrupt flights
items.desc: Houthi attacks have disrupted nearly half of scheduled flights from Saudi airports, leaving migrant workers without clear information as their leave runs out and exit-re-entry permits near expiry.

items.title: The government should stop intimidating journalists
items.desc: Raids on newsrooms and arrests of reporters have no place in a democracy that guarantees press freedom.

items.title: Sudurpaschim Royals break silence on Saturday night delays and absence from post-match conference
items.desc: Head coach Misbah-ul-Haq clarifies his squad’s stance following an hour-long administrative delay that culminated in a 35-run defeat to Biratnagar Kings.

items.title: Jumla’s prized Marsi rice is in demand, but production is declining
items.desc: From village kitchens to urban hotels and international markets, demand for the indigenous rice is rising, but pest outbreaks and rising cultivation costs are adding to farmers’ woes.

items.title: Nationwide micronutrients survey to be carried out next month
items.desc: Officials had planned to postpone the regular vitamin A supplementation and deworming campaign until March next year so they could know the actual prevalence of vitamin A deficiency if the supplement is not given before the study.

items.title: Gagan Thapa signals a more assertive role for Congress as main opposition
items.desc: President says the party will no longer just issue statements over government actions; it would make a more concerted effort in favour of press freedom, judicial independence and the economy.

items.title: Sudurpaschim showers state funds on temples, skimps on free medicines
items.desc: The provincial government has allocated funds for 921 temples, while public health facilities face a severe shortage of funds to buy essential medicines.

items.title: Many children of Nepal’s Maoist war are done with politics
items.desc: Two decades after the insurgency ended, the children of Nepal’s Maoist fighters are building careers in IT, fashion and insurance. A few still carry the cause.

items.title: Janakpur register second win in three games
items.desc: Trit Raj Das’s 61 helps Janakpur defend a modest 147-run total as Pokhara fall nine runs short and suffer their second defeat of the season.

items.title: Janakpur Bolts beat Pokhara Avengers by nine runs for second straight win
items.desc: Trit Raj Das’s half-century helped Janakpur defend a target of 148, while Moeen Ali took three wickets as Pokhara suffered their second consecutive defeat.

items.title: Rosha Phuyel’s devotion to bhajan finds new admirers
items.desc: Many listeners discovered the teenager’s mellifluous voice through her recent rendition of the classic bhajan ‘Jai Ambe’. But she has been at it for some time—and is in it for the long haul.

items.title: Janakpur Bolts set Pokhara Avengers a target of 148
items.desc: Tritraj Das top-scored with 61 as Janakpur posted 147 for six in their 20 overs.

items.title: Bangladesh forms wage board as garment protests turn violent
items.desc: Bangladesh’s ready-made garment industry, the world’s largest after China, contributes about 10 percent of gross domestic product and is the backbone of ​the economy.

items.title: Thousands join Indian opposition protest demanding poll chief’s resignation
items.desc: Led by Congress party chief Rahul Gandhi, Sunday’s protesters say the controversial revision benefits Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya ​Janata Party.

items.title: Janakpur Bolts and Pokhara Avengers meet as NPL returns to action
items.desc: With clear weather and the wet outfield now dry, Sunday’s match at TU International Cricket Ground is expected to start on schedule after rain disrupted Saturday’s fixtures.

items.title: Supreme Court orders government to regulate cannabis cultivation for medicinal and industrial use
items.desc: The court has given the government three months to introduce regulations, licensing requirements and monitoring mechanisms for controlled commercial cultivation, while calling for wider consultations on recreational use.

items.title: Kathmandu Film Festival screening new titles and restored classics
items.desc: The three-day festival features 38 films from 14 countries, alongside heritage events, masterclasses and discussions on the future of cinema.

items.title: Young trekker found dead near Badimalika
items.desc: The 20-year-old from Kanchanpur was found near Triveni Patan after snowfall and freezing temperatures hit the area

items.title: Four Nepali Americans seek seats in three US state legislatures
items.desc: The four Democratic candidates are running in Maryland, New Hampshire and New York in the November 3 midterm elections.

items.title: Eight inmates escape Dolpa prison through tunnel dug beneath compound
items.desc: The escape, three days after a new duty in-charge was assigned, has raised questions about prison security and surveillance. Five of the escapees were serving sentences for rape cases, and three were involved in theft cases.

items.title: Eight injured in fire at steel factory in Banke
items.desc: An electrical short circuit in three furnaces triggered the blaze at Ambe Steels in Janaki Rural Municipality. Two of the injured have been referred to Lucknow for further treatment.

items.title: Indian authorities tighten security ahead of big opposition march in Delhi
items.desc: Police deploy riot-control units and announce traffic diversions as Rahul Gandhi leads a protest demanding the election chief’s resignation over controversial voter-list revisions.

items.title: Army helicopter to rescue six Indian tourists stranded by snow in Dolpa
items.desc: The tourists are stranded in Danigad of Shey Phoksundo Rural Municipality as several days of heavy snowfall disrupt life in the high Himalayan region.

items.title: Bad weather disrupts flights at several airports; two international flights diverted
items.desc: Bharatpur, Surkhet and Bhairahawa airports remain closed, while poor visibility and low cloud cover affect operations at Kathmandu airport.

items.title: Parsa stakeholders agree on joint efforts to clean up polluted Sirsiya river
items.desc: Industries along the Parsa-Bara industrial corridor will be barred from discharging untreated wastewater into the river and required to operate treatment plants around the clock.

items.title: Nepali players take the lead in NPL’s Player of the Match awards
items.desc: After two seasons of an even split, Nepali cricketers have edged ahead of overseas players, winning 38 of the 70 awards handed out so far.

items.title: Bangladesh to form wage board after garment protests shut factories
items.desc: Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka, more than double the current rate, as factory closures and clashes with police disrupt production in the country’s biggest export industry.

items.title: Bankers fear loan misuse ruling could shake confidence in lending
items.desc: With excess liquidity, historically low interest rates and weak credit demand, bankers warn that the prospect of criminal cases against borrowers who divert loan funds could further dampen lending, particularly if past loans are affected.
